<!--
Step 04 of the workflow. Computes two indicators from the PAIRED scenario ensembles
produced by 03_Scenarios_Through_time.Rmd (saved as sims_factual / sims_counter):
  (1) per-species MEAN INDIVIDUAL WEIGHT through time (size-structure indicator),
      factual (seal increase) vs counterfactual (seals held at 1978);
  (2) MODEL SKILL = Spearman correlation of modelled vs observed biomass across the
      ensemble, factual vs counterfactual.
Current dimensions: 1978-2024 (47 yr), all 19 species, per-species survey cutoffs.
(Journal style: no plot titles/subtitles; notes/interpretation as comments.)
-->

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(here)
library(mizer)
library(mizerExperimental)
library(tidyverse)
library(patchwork)
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = here::here())   # portable project root
save_dir <- paste0(here::here(), "/Ess_Output/")
knitr::opts_chunk$set(message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
```

## Inputs — factual model + paired scenario ensembles (from step 03)

```{r inputs}
# Factual Stage-2 model (for species set + per-species survey cutoffs)
params <- readRDS(if (file.exists("Ess_data/params_stage2_AUTO.RDS"))
                    "Ess_data/params_stage2_AUTO.RDS" else
                    "Ess_data/params_stage2_factual.RDS")

# Paired ensembles from 03 (same randomised web under both scenarios):
#   sims_factual = seal effort increases 1978->2024
#   sims_counter = seal effort held constant at the 1978 level (the counterfactual)
sims_factual <- readRDS("Ess_Output/sims_factual.RDS")
sims_counter <- readRDS("Ess_Output/sims_counter.RDS")

# Observed survey biomass (g) for the skill comparison
biomass_ts <- readRDS("Ess_data/biomass_ts.RDS")

sp    <- species_params(params)$species
cl    <- species_params(params)$biomass_cutoff;     cl[is.na(cl)] <- 0    # lower survey cutoff
ch    <- species_params(params)$biomass_cutoffHigh; ch[is.na(ch)] <- Inf  # upper survey cutoff
w     <- params@w; dw <- params@dw
n_sims <- length(sims_factual)
cat(sprintf("Ensemble size: %d factual, %d counterfactual paired members\n",
            length(sims_factual), length(sims_counter)))
```

# Read abundance by species
```{r}
# read abundance by species (survey numbers per species-year)
abundance_obs <- read.csv("Ess_data/abundance_obs.csv")
# Make sure Species types match for the join
abundance_long <- abundance_obs %>%
  mutate(Species = factor(Species, levels = levels(biomass_ts$Species)))

# Join and compute mean weight
mean_weight_ts <- biomass_ts %>%
  left_join(abundance_long, by = c("Year", "Species")) %>%
  mutate(MeanWeight = Biomass / Abundance)
```


## Per-sim indicators (biomass, numbers, mean weight) above the survey cutoff

```{r indicator-helper}
# For one MizerSim: per species & year, biomass and numbers WITHIN that species'
# survey size window [biomass_cutoff, biomass_cutoffHigh] (comparable to the survey,
# which misses both the smallest AND the largest fish), mean individual weight =
# biomass / numbers (g). The UPPER cutoff is essential: without it a collapsed stock's
# few huge old survivors inflate mean weight far above the survey (cod 2024: 23 kg
# lower-only vs ~23 g within-window). Returns long data.frame.
sim_indicators <- function(sim) {
  st <- as.integer(dimnames(sim@n)[[1]])
  do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(sp), function(j) {
    idx <- w >= cl[j] & w <= ch[j]
    B <- rowSums(sweep(sim@n[, j, idx, drop = FALSE], 3, (w * dw)[idx], "*"))  # g
    N <- rowSums(sweep(sim@n[, j, idx, drop = FALSE], 3,  dw[idx],      "*"))  # numbers
    data.frame(Species = sp[j], Year = st, Biomass = B, Number = N,
               MeanWeight = B / N)
  }))
}

# Apply across an ensemble, tagging the sim index and scenario.
ensemble_indicators <- function(sims, scenario) {
  do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(sims), function(k) {
    d <- sim_indicators(sims[[k]]); d$sim <- k; d$scen <- scenario; d
  }))
}

df_all <- bind_rows(
  ensemble_indicators(sims_factual, "Factual (seal increase)"),
  ensemble_indicators(sims_counter, "Counterfactual (seals constant)"))

```

```{r}
# ── READ & PREPARE OBSERVED MEAN WEIGHT ──────────────────────────────────────
abundance_obs <- read.csv("Ess_data/abundance_obs.csv")

# Match Species factor levels to biomass_ts so the join works cleanly
abundance_long <- abundance_obs %>%
  mutate(Species = factor(Species, levels = levels(biomass_ts$Species)))

# Join biomass and abundance, compute observed mean individual weight (g)
mean_weight_ts <- biomass_ts %>%
  left_join(abundance_long, by = c("Year", "Species")) %>%
  mutate(MeanWeight = Biomass / Abundance) %>%        # Biomass in g, Abundance in numbers
  filter(!is.na(MeanWeight), MeanWeight > 0,          # drop missing / zero
         is.finite(MeanWeight))                        # drop Inf from zero abundance
```

## Indicator 1 — mean individual weight per species, factual vs counterfactual

```{r mean-weight}
# Ensemble median + 10-90% band (the band is the ensemble spread across randomised
# food webs, NOT a formal CI). Factual vs counterfactual overlaid per species.
# ── SUMMARISE ENSEMBLE ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
mw <- df_all %>%
  group_by(scen, Species, Year) %>%
  summarise(med = median(MeanWeight),
            lo  = quantile(MeanWeight, 0.10),
            hi  = quantile(MeanWeight, 0.90), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(Species = factor(Species, levels = levels(mean_weight_ts$Species))) %>%
  arrange(Species, Year)

# ── PLOT ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
p_mw <- ggplot(mw, aes(Year, med, colour = scen, fill = scen)) +

  # Ensemble spread (10–90% band)
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), alpha = 0.20, colour = NA) +

  # Ensemble median lines
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.6) +

  # Observed mean weight — black points, separate data layer
  geom_point(
    data        = mean_weight_ts,          # already filtered above
    aes(x = Year, y = MeanWeight),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    colour      = "black",
    shape       = 16,
    size        = 0.8
  ) +

  facet_wrap(~ Species, scales = "free_y") +

  scale_colour_manual(
    values = c("Factual (seal increase)"         = "firebrick",
               "Counterfactual (seals constant)" = "steelblue")
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c("Factual (seal increase)"         = "firebrick",
               "Counterfactual (seals constant)" = "steelblue")
  ) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 9) +
  labs(x = "Year", y = "Mean individual weight (g)") +
  theme(
    text             = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
    axis.title       = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
    axis.text.y      = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold"),
    axis.text.x      = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold"),
    legend.title     = element_blank(),
    legend.text      = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold"),
    legend.position  = "bottom",
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.border     = element_rect(linewidth = 1),
    panel.grid.major = element_blank()
  )

p_mw
ggsave(paste0(save_dir, "indicator_mean_weight.jpeg"),
       p_mw, width = 14, height = 10, dpi = 200)

# INTERPRETATION (comment): where the counterfactual (blue) sits above the factual (red),
# removing the seal increase leaves larger mean body size (less size-selective seal
# predation + recovered large fish). Bands = 10-90% of ensemble webs.
```


## Indicator 2 — model skill (modelled vs observed biomass) by scenario

```{r model-skill}
# Observed survey biomass and catches per species-year
obs <- biomass_ts |> transmute(Species, Year, Biomass_obs = Biomass / 1e9)
obs_catch <- readRDS("Ess_data/yield_ts.RDS") |>
  filter(!Species %in% c("Sand Lance", "Capelin", "Longhorn Sculpin")) |>
  transmute(Species, Year, Yield_obs = Yield / 1e9)

# Modelled fishing catch per ensemble member (sum over fishing gears, excl. Seals) — g
fish_gears <- c("Bottom_Trawl", "Fixed_Gear", "Small_Mesh", "Pelagic")
sim_catch <- function(sim) {
  yg <- getYieldGear(sim)                                   # [time, gear, species]
  fy <- apply(yg[, dimnames(yg)[[2]] %in% fish_gears, , drop = FALSE], c(1, 3), sum)
  st <- as.integer(rownames(fy))
  do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(sp),
    function(j) data.frame(Species = sp[j], Year = st, Yield = fy[, j])))
}
ensemble_catch <- function(sims, scenario) {
  do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(sims), function(k) {
    d <- sim_catch(sims[[k]]); d$sim <- k; d$scen <- scenario; d }))
}
df_catches <- bind_rows(
  ensemble_catch(sims_factual, "Factual (seal increase)"),
  ensemble_catch(sims_counter, "Counterfactual (seals constant)"))

# Per ensemble member: Spearman rho for biomass
skill_biomass <- df_all |>
  mutate(Biomass = Biomass / 1e9) |>
  inner_join(obs, by = c("Species", "Year")) |>
  filter(Biomass_obs > 0, Biomass > 0) |>
  group_by(scen, sim) |>
  summarise(rho_biomass = cor(Biomass, Biomass_obs, method = "spearman"), .groups = "drop")

# Per ensemble member: Spearman rho for catches
skill_catch <- df_catches |>
  mutate(Yield = Yield / 1e9) |>
  inner_join(obs_catch, by = c("Species", "Year")) |>
  filter(Yield_obs > 0, Yield > 0) |>
  group_by(scen, sim) |>
  summarise(rho_catch = cor(Yield, Yield_obs, method = "spearman"), .groups = "drop")

# Per ensemble member: Spearman rho for mean individual weight
# (no observed counterpart — cross-scenario comparison only: factual vs counterfactual)
skill_mw <- df_all |>
  filter(!is.na(MeanWeight), MeanWeight > 0) |>
  group_by(scen, sim) |>
  summarise(rho_mw = cor(MeanWeight, Year, method = "spearman"), .groups = "drop")
# Note: rho_mw here is the trend correlation (weight ~ year) per scenario/sim.
# A positive rho = mean weight increasing over time; negative = declining.
# The difference between scenarios isolates the seal effect on body size.

# Combine all three skill metrics
skill <- left_join(skill_biomass, skill_catch, by = c("scen", "sim")) |>
  left_join(skill_mw, by = c("scen", "sim")) |>
  pivot_longer(cols = c(rho_biomass, rho_catch, rho_mw),
               names_to = "indicator", values_to = "rho") |>
  mutate(indicator = recode(indicator,
    "rho_biomass" = "Biomass",
    "rho_catch"   = "Catch",
    "rho_mw"      = "Mean individual weight"))

p_sk <- ggplot(skill, aes(scen, rho, fill = scen)) +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.6, outlier.size = 0.3) +
  facet_wrap(~ indicator) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Factual (seal increase)"         = "red",
                               "Counterfactual (seals constant)" = "blue")) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Spearman rho (modelled vs observed)") +
  theme(legend.position = "none",
        strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"))+
  theme_bw() +
  theme(
    text = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold"),
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold"),
    legend.title = element_blank(),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold"),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.border = element_rect(linewidth = 1),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())
ggsave("plot.png", p_sk, width = 10, height = 5, dpi = 300)
ggsave(paste0(save_dir, "indicator_model_skill.jpeg"), p_sk, width = 14, height = 5, dpi = 200)
p_sk

# Median skill per scenario and indicator across the ensemble
skill |> group_by(scen, indicator) |>
  summarise(median_rho = round(median(rho), 3),
            q10 = round(quantile(rho, 0.10), 3),
            q90 = round(quantile(rho, 0.90), 3), .groups = "drop")
# INTERPRETATION (comment): three-panel skill plot — biomass, catch, mean weight.
# Biomass and catch rho = Spearman correlation of modelled vs observed pattern.
# Mean weight rho = temporal trend (weight ~ year) per scenario; difference between
# scenarios isolates the seal effect on community body size structure.
# Higher biomass/catch rho = better fit to data; mean weight panel shows direction
# and consistency of the size-structure response to the seal increase.

# INTERPRETATION (comment): higher rho = better reproduction of the observed biomass
# pattern. If the factual (seal-increase) scenario has higher skill than the
# counterfactual, the data favour the seal-increase mechanism.

```
